einzeiler: How Matt Ross lost everything at 50 and chose growth over folding to rebuild his life.
kurzfassung: Matt Ross built a global brand with School of Rock before facing a catastrophic convergence of personal and professional crises at age 50. Sitting alone in his basement, he chose growth over folding, fundamentally shifting his approach to life and business. He shares how treating oneself like a business and pursuing creative growth became the foundation for his recovery.
stichpunkte: Matt Ross grew up in a dysfunctional Queens household with divorcing parents and an abusive environment.
He built a successful career in media advertising before scaling School of Rock globally.
At age 50, he faced five major simultaneous crises: losing his company, health issues, aging parents, struggling brothers, and his son's severe psychiatric breakdown.
Sitting in his basement, he rejected defeat and coined the personal mantra "Grow or Fold."
He sought professional help, enrolled in Al-Anon, and successfully found residential care for his autistic son.
Treating himself like a business provided a structured strategy with clear, measurable goals.
He later founded One River School, building 15 art schools across six states.
He emphasizes the importance of functional, emotional, and creative growth for lifelong well-being.

clips.text: He has always practiced radical transparency in his relationships and professional life, though he has had to adjust his expectations of others who operate differently.
Within his fiftieth year, his son experienced a psychiatric emergency, his brothers struggled with addiction, his parents declined, and he lost his company simultaneously.

clips.hook: Why ego stops us from asking for help
clips.text: Societal pressures and personal pride often prevent individuals from admitting vulnerability and seeking guidance when they are completely overwhelmed.

clips.hook: Beating yourself up over minor mistakes
clips.text: He describes how he used to punish himself mentally for tiny errors despite achieving major successes, lacking any internal mechanism for self-compassion.

clips.hook: Improv comedy and cabaret singing at 65
clips.text: To inject more joy into his daily routine, he recently returned to his creative roots by taking improv and singing classes.

beschreibung:
Maybe you’ve had a moment where you looked around at your life and didn’t recognize it. Not because it was bad, exactly. But because everything you’d been holding together had finally stopped holding. That moment has a weight to it that’s hard to describe. And if you’ve been there, this episode is going to feel familiar.

Matt Ross spent decades building things. He grew School of Rock from a struggling startup into a global brand. He led teams, created value, stayed in motion. He was the guy with the plan. And then at fifty, everything came apart at the same time. His son had a psychiatric breakdown. His brothers were lost to addiction. Both sets of parents were dying. He’d just lost the company he’d built. And one night he sat alone in his basement and asked himself if he was going to fold.

He didn’t fold. But the road back wasn’t fast or clean or dramatic. It was therapy, Al-Anon, medication, a very slow kind of self-honesty, and eventually, a question that changed everything: what if you treated yourself like a business? This conversation is about what it actually looks like to rebuild from the inside out, one careful step at a time.

What You’ll Hear:

The moment Matt sat in his basement and asked himself if he would fold

What it felt like to carry the weight of a disabled son, addicted brothers, and dying parents all at once

Why treating yourself like a business became the framework that helped him rebuild

The slow, unglamorous work of therapy, Al-Anon, and learning to ask for help

How founding One River School gave him the first real sense of purpose he’d ever felt

What he means by functional, emotional, and creative growth, and why creative growth might be the missing piece for a lot of us

Guest Bio:

Matt Ross is an entrepreneur, author, and media executive with nearly 30 years of experience building businesses that inspire passion and creativity. From rocking New York’s airwaves to scaling global education brands, now he is the author of GROW OR FOLD: Transform Yourself in Midlife and Beyond, a profound story of awakening your enthusiasm for growth.

Since 2012, Matt has been the Founder and CEO of One River School, a company whose mission is to “Transform Art Education®.” Today, One River operates fifteen schools in six states with plans for substantial growth over the next five years.

Learn more at mattross.com
